sims.title: Soliton crystal with a vacancy
sims.caption: Five pulses of light circle the ring at equal spacing, held apart by the ripples each one leaves behind. One site is deliberately left empty, and that vacancy prints itself as a fingerprint on the output spectrum.

sims.title: Breathing solitons
sims.caption: Push the drive a little harder and the pulses stop sitting still: they swell and shrink in a steady rhythm, over and over. Breathers like these are how a soliton loses its balance without falling apart.

sims.title: A single cavity soliton
sims.caption: One pulse, alone in the cavity. It keeps its shape indefinitely because nonlinearity compresses it exactly as fast as dispersion spreads it, while the laser drive replaces the light lost on every round trip.

figures.alt: Isosurfaces of three-dimensional light bullets and their higher-order relatives in a Kerr cavity with a parabolic potential.
figures.caption: Light can be trapped in all three directions at once, making a bullet of energy that holds together as it circulates. A gentle lens-like potential keeps even the fragile higher-order shapes from collapsing.

figures.alt: Simulated intensity map of a parametrically driven temporal soliton crystal in a doubly resonant fibre cavity.
figures.caption: Drive a cavity at twice the light's own frequency and its pulses lock into an evenly spaced ring, like beads on a necklace. Some crystals never settle: the pulses take turns brightening and chasing one another.

figures.alt: Measured and simulated time traces of two multimode solitons colliding inside a graded-index optical fibre.
figures.caption: In a fibre that guides many shapes of light at once, two pulses can drift towards each other and collide. The collision is not gentle: the trailing pulse steals energy, then races away from its neighbour.

figures.alt: Hermite-Gaussian mode profiles of a photonic-crystal nanolaser and the pulse train they build up.
figures.caption: A laser barely wider than a human hair can be shaped so that its modes march in step, turning a steady glow into a train of pulses. The cavity behaves like a quantum harmonic oscillator made of light.
